text:
- [LTHE.2.2.2] Match Y such that `Y.ts > X.ts` (strictly after)
  and `Y.ts - X.ts < T` (within the bound).

  Both comparisons are on the facts' `ts` values — when the events happened —
  not on when the engine received them. A sequence's order and window are
  therefore event time, and the monotonic clock takes no part in them
  ([LTIM.2.8.2]). A fact delivered late still orders by its `ts`, and a wall
  clock step between two facts whose `ts` the engine filled can invert their
  order, as it can for any two `ts` values.

idris.name: Lthe_2_2_2__event
idris.note: A fact as a sequence sees it: its `ts`, when the event happened, and its entry stamp, when the engine received it ([LTIM.2.8.6]).

idris.name: iret_19_5__by_clock_is_time_dependent
idris.note: 'The comparisons are on the facts' `ts` values, and the monotonic clock takes no part in them': the window measured on the clock instead changes as the clock advances, the facts unchanged. Computed.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__late_delivery_still_matches
idris.note: A FACT DELIVERED LATE STILL MATCHES BY ITS `ts`: X happened at 1 and arrived at 1, Y happened at 2 and arrived at 50; by event time Y is within 10 of X, by arrival it is not. 'A fact delivered late still orders by its `ts`', computed.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__prompt_delivery_does_not
idris.note: AND ONE DELIVERED AT ONCE WHOSE EVENT WAS LONG AFTER does the reverse: Y happened at 100 and arrived at 2. Computed; the two tests are not one test.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__sequence
idris.note: THE SEQUENCE'S TEST, on `ts` alone: Y strictly after X, and within the bound. The clause's two comparisons, on the facts' own `ts`.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__sequence_by_arrival
idris.note: THE REFUSED READING: the same test on the entry stamps, when the engine received the facts.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__wall_step_inverts
idris.note: A WALL CLOCK STEP INVERTS THE ORDER of two facts the engine emitted at consecutive steps: with the source whose wall clock goes back, (1, 9) then (2, 4), the fact emitted second is the earlier event, and the sequence matches the two in that order and not in the order of emission. The clause's last sentence, computed.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__tick_leaves_chain
idris.note: The monotonic clock takes no part: a tick's re-evaluation leaves a sequence chain as it was.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__tick_leaves_engine
idris.note: The monotonic clock takes no part: a tick leaves the engine whose one chain is a sequence.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__ts
idris.note: The `ts` the clause compares, as the model carries it.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__untimed
idris.note: A sequence program carries no time-dependent test for the tick to re-evaluate. A fixture.

idris.name: lthe_2_2_2__within
idris.note: `Y.ts > X.ts` and `Y.ts - X.ts < T`, on the facts' `ts` values and on nothing else; the monotonic clock takes no part because the test cannot read it.

idris.name: lthe_2_3_1__within_at
idris.note: `Y.ts > X.ts` and `Y.ts - X.ts < T` with X the token's fact at a rank.

idris.name: lthe_2_3_1__within_from
idris.note: The two comparisons on `ts`, against a fact given or absent.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__inputs
idris.note: Facts at their event times, with a clock tick past all of them between arrivals: the window is on `ts`, not on arrival. A fixture.

idris.name: lthe_2_5_1__two_pairs
idris.note: The pairs the clause admits, executed: strictly after and within the bound on `ts`; the tick past every `ts` changed none. Computed.
